title: Yao et al. 2023: close-in pressures on a 4 x 5 m slab's top face
summary: 0.5 and 1 kg of TNT hung 0.8 to 1 m over the centre of a 4 x 5 m, 150 mm reinforced concrete slab (0.8 to 1.26 m/kg^(1/3)): the peak pressure on its top face under the charge and 1 m out. The slab barely moved (under a millimetre), so the load is the test here.

sources.title: Dynamic response and damage characteristics of large reinforced concrete slabs under explosion
sources.used_for: The slab, the tests and the top-face peak pressures read off Figure 6b

obstacles.description: Simply supported on its two long sides on L-shaped concrete supports (150 mm bearing). Treated as rigid for the load: T1-T3 left no visible damage and moved under 1 mm.

notes: The paper also reports underside displacements and accelerations. They are left out: the reported displacements (0.35-0.86 mm, taken at the wave's arrival) are not comparable with a slab's whole swing, and the displacement record's own meaning is unclear.
A fourth test, 20 kg at 1 m on a second slab, damaged it (a 1.02 x 0.76 m top crater); it has no measured pressure or deflection and is left out.
